THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA, PRAYING TO QUASH THE PRELIMINARY NOTIFICATION DATED 26.11.1959 GAZETTED ON 28.01.1960 ISSUED UNDER SEC. 4(1) AND FINAL NOTIFICATION DATED 28.9.1965 ISSUED UNDER SEC. 6 OF THE LAND ACQUISITION ACT, 1894 IN RESPECT OF THE PETITIONER'S LAND BEARING SY.NO.26/1 MEASURING 5 ACRES 3 GUNTAS, SITUATED AT JAKKASANDRA VILLAGE,
BEGUR HOBLI, BENGALURU SOUTH TALUK AT ANNEX-D & E AND ETC.,
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Petitioner claiming to be the successor in title of the subject lands is knocking at the doors of writ court for laying a challenge to the acquisition that had commenced with the issuance of Preliminary Notification dated 26.11.1959 u/s.4(1) followed by the Final Notification dated 28.09.1965 issued u/s.6 of the erstwhile Land Acquisition Act, 1984.
2.

Learned Sr. Advocate appearing for the petitioner seeks to void the acquisition on the grounds that: possession of the land continues with his client even after award was passed before 01.01.2009 and therefore the proceedings have lapsed u/s.24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and u/s.27 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976; despite award no compensation has been paid to the land owner under whom petitioner claims as the relinquishee.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Lastly, the subject lands have been de-notified u/s.48 of the 1894 Act vide Notification dated 14.12.2009.

3. After service of notice the State has entered appearance through the learned AGA and the BDA has entered appearance through its learned Sr. Panel Counsel who has filed his Statement of Objections on 20.09.2017.

Both the AGA and the Panel Counsel make submission in justification of Sri Srinivas Murthy V vs The State Of Karnataka on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10884517/
2 the impugned notifications and thereby resist the writ petition.

entities.text: Sri Srinivas Murthy V vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They plead about absence of petitioner's locus standii and enormous delay of decades in filing the writ petition with no plausible explanation.
Lastly, they notify to the court the cases fought upto the level of Apex Court unsuccessfully in laying a challenge to the acquisition in question.

4. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having perused the petition papers, this Court declines indulgence in the matter for the following reasons:
(a) The petition land admeasuring 5 acres & 3 guntas was situate in Sy.No.26/1 at Jakkasandra village, Bengaluru South Taluka.
The acquisition process began with the issuance of Preliminary Notification dated 26.11.1959 followed by the Final Notification dated 28.09.1965 respectively issued u/ss.4(1) & 6(1) of the 1894 Act.
Sec.5A enquiry was held in which the land owner Mr.R.Hanumaiah had filed his objections after service of notice dated 10.12.1965.
Thereafter the award was passed on 06.11.1969; the Government granted the approval on the same day; the petitioner had sought for enhancement of compensation.
He received the compensation with the voucher signed and under protest vide representation dated 12.03.1976.
Therefore whatever be the arguable interest of the petitioner in the subject land, he has no locus standii to invoke judicial process for voiding the acquisition.

Added,
there is a enormous delay a little less than six decades and the explanation offered for the same is militantly short of being plausible, to say the least.

(b) The CITB, i.e., the predecessor of respondent- BDA had passed resolutions dated 26.06.1968 and 19.04.1972 for reconveying inter alia the subject land to Mr. Hanumaiah even after formation of the layout.
However these resolutions were not given effect to.
Mr.Hanumaiah had filed W.P.No.15487/1987 seeking a direction to the BDA for reconveying the same in terms of those resolutions.
However, a co-ordinate Bench of this Court dismissed the same vide judgment dated 03.04.1989.
His W.A.No.727/1989 filed against the same was allowed on 09.07.2011.

However in BDA's Civil Appeal No.971/2003 the Apex Court reversed the same vide order dated 03.10.2005,
however directing grant of enhanced compensation at the rate of Rs.19,000/- per acre.
This amount was deposited in the Court.

(c) Mr. R. Hanumaiah had filed W.P No. 26826/2005 calling in question the validity of vires of section 9 of Act 17 of 1994 which validated the CIDB allotments made during the period between 20.12.1973 and 08.05.1986.
In the meanwhile, the State Government by its Notification dated 14.10.2009, issued u/s 48(1) of the 1894 Act, had denotified inter alia the petition land.

Therefore,
Hanumaiah's W.P.No.26826/2005 came to be disposed off.
The denotification was challenged by some of the allottees of sites in W.P.Nos.32919-922/2009.
The State Government issued another Notification dated 13.11.2009 rescinding the said denotification.
This was challenged by Mr.Hanumaiah in W.P.No.21186/2010 that came to be dismissed on 20.04.2012.
For the same reason, the site allottees W.P.Nos.32919-922/2009 also came to be dismissed as having become infructuous.

sentences.text: (d) Mr.Hanumaiah filed W.A.Nos.3051-3067/2012 against the order dated 20.04.2012 made in his W.P.No.21186/2010.

The Division Bench had allowed the said appeal in part on 10.12.2014 by quashing the Withdrawal Notification and remanding the matter to the State Government for consideration afresh, after hearing the parties.

BDA preferred SLP (C) Nos.13235- 13252/2015 which later came to be registered as Civil Appeal Nos.2576-2593/2017, which came to be allowed by the Apex Court vide order dated 12.05.2017 imposing a heavy cost of Rs.5,00,000/- on the L.Rs of deceased R.Hanumaiah.
The petitioner has not whispered one single sentence about all this in his pleadings.
It is impossible to believe that he did not have knowledge of the same.
Merely trumpeting that he belongs to Scheduled Caste, would not do.
Litigants of this kind cannot go unscathed.
A strong message should go to potential litigants of the kind that the courts would not let such persons go with impunity.
They should be made to cough up huge costs, having exemplary elements, regard being had to Apex Court's levy of penal cost of Rs.5,00,000/-.
(e) The vehement submission of learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner that his client has been continuing in the possession of the property even to this day, cannot be believed.
The compensation having been received by Mr.Hanumaiah under protest inasmuch as he has sought for enhancement of compensation vide application dated 12.03.1976.

Mr.Hanumaiah S/o Munigurappa under whom the Petitioner claims, has executed a document dated 23.12.1966 at Annexure-R4 to the Statement of Objections, wherein he has specifically stated that he is not the rightful owner, the true owner being R.Hanumaiah.
Mr.R.Hanumaiah under whom the Petitioner claims had made a petition dated 23.12.1966 requesting the authorities to drop the acquisition proceedings.
The knowledge of the proceedings therefore has to be attributed to the Petitioner who claims under him, as rightly contended by the learned Panel Counsel appearing for the BDA.
(f) This apart, if the Petitioner has any grievance, as to the fraud allegedly committed by some other person with the name of Mr.Hanumaiah, his remedy lies elsewhere.
Nothing enures to the benefit of Petitioner by virtue of registered lease deed dated 16.03.2017 at Annexure-C in the light of what has been discussed above.
The said document runs counter to the orders of this court and of Apex Court of the country.
Such conveyances - 10 - brought about by connivance deserve to be condemned to the dustbin, to say the least.

(g) The vehement submission of learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner that Petitioner is entitled to have the benefit of statutory lapse of acquisition in terms of Section 24(2) of 2013 Act, is not tenable, in view of acquiescence or Mr.Hanumaiah in the acquisition by taking the compensation, of course with protest, the said protest being confined to his right to seek higher compensation.

As already observed above, the possession of the land was taken, way back on 3.3.1975 by the CITB; the layout was formed and sites have been allotted to several others; in such a situation, the law declared by the Apex Court in GOVERNMENT OF NCT OF DELHI VS. MOHD.
ZUBAIR (2023) 1 SCC 174, come to the rescue of Respondents.

As already mentioned above, the said Writ Petition came to be disposed off as having become infructuous since the denotification was withdrawn by the State Government by another Notification dated 13.11.2009.

The beneficiaries of allotment who are proper parties if not necessary parties in the light of RAZIA BEGUM vs. SAHEBZADI ANWAR BEGUM AIR 1958 SC 886 have not been arraigned as parties to the petition nor any explanation is offered for not impleading them.
